clue.text: Withdrawing support of force

parts.note: backing is support, as given to a cause or a candidate
F is the standard abbreviation for force in physics

explanation.surface: Someone pulls their backing from a military or police force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support of force' reads as one phrase about a force being supported, but each word is its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To back off is to retreat or climb down, so backing off is pulling back from a position.

clue.text: Make prediction about opener for live band

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the wager wraps round the letter

parts.note: to bet is to predict an outcome and stake money on it

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Fans predict which song a live band will open with.
explanation.walkthrough: BET goes round L, the first letter of 'live'.
explanation.definitionFit: A belt is a strip or band, as of leather round the waist or a belt of land.

clue.text: Eatery in Corsica regularly hosting a gala

indicators.note: hosting means having guests inside, so the picked letters hold the next pieces
regularly means taking letters at even intervals, here the first, third, fifth and seventh

parts.note: a fete is a festive gala, often an outdoor fundraising event

explanation.surface: A restaurant in Corsica often holds a gala.
explanation.walkthrough: Every other letter of 'Corsica' gives CRIA, which holds A and FETE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafeteria is a self-service restaurant, one kind of eatery.

clue.text: One sister nice in false pretences

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: false means not genuine, so these letters are rearranged into a different word

explanation.surface: A nun's niceness is put on, all pretence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is the Roman numeral, kept outside the anagram that 'false' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Insincerities are things said or shown without real feeling, i.e. pretences.

clue.text: Foolish East German ignoring an indicator of fuel use

indicators.note: foolish suggests muddled thinking, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A daft East German pays no attention to the fuel gauge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foolish' jumbles EAST GERMAN, and 'ignoring an' takes A and N out of that pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas meter measures how much gas a household burns, so it shows fuel consumption.

clue.text: Raw meat changing hands

indicators.note: the hands are left and right, so the letter for one is swapped for the letter for the other

parts.note: flesh is the soft tissue of an animal, i.e. meat

explanation.surface: Raw meat is passed from one owner to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing hands' swaps the L (left) in FLESH for R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh food is uncooked or unprocessed, so fresh and raw are close synonyms.

clue.text: Leave queen, maybe spades? Not spades!

parts.note: Q is the abbreviation for queen, as on playing cards

indicators.note: Not followed by the item to drop tells us to take that letter out of the word just found

parts.note: spades are one example of a suit in a pack of cards, hence 'maybe'
S is the abbreviation for spades in card notation

explanation.surface: A card player muses whether to lead the queen of spades, then rejects spades.
explanation.walkthrough: The SUIT that spades exemplifies loses its S, the abbreviation for spades, leaving UIT after Q.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit a place or a job is to leave it; the two verbs are plain synonyms.

clue.text: One including learner that's not illuminated

indicators.note: including means taking in, so the first word holds the letter

parts.note: a unit is a single thing, i.e. one
L is the abbreviation for learner, as on L-plates for learner drivers

explanation.surface: A student among the group is left in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: UNIT takes in L.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlit means without light, so not lit up or illuminated.

clue.text: Cool tip I note to cut hair

indicators.note: to cut into is to go inside, so these pieces sit within the hair

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair
an end is a tip, as of a pencil

explanation.surface: A stylish tip: get a note to the hairdresser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cool' reads as an adjective but is the noun, coolness. END, I and N cut TRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendiness is being fashionable, which is what being cool, as a noun, means in the slang sense.

clue.text: Pigeon sheds frequently seen in outskirts of Leeds

indicators.note: something seen in a place sits inside it, so these letters go within the outer pair
the outskirts of a town are its edges, so we keep only the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: oft is an old word for often, i.e. frequently

explanation.surface: Pigeon lofts are a common sight on the edges of the northern English city of Leeds.
explanation.walkthrough: The outskirts of Leeds are L and S, which hold OFT.
explanation.definitionFit: A loft is the raised shed or roost where racing pigeons are kept, a sense special to pigeon fanciers.

clue.text: Sounding appropriate, depressed tone

indicators.note: Sounding tells us to take a word for how it is said rather than how it is spelt

parts.note: as a verb, to appropriate is to take for oneself, i.e. to steal
feeling blue means feeling low or depressed

explanation.surface: Someone's voice sounds fitting but has a downbeat tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' looks like the adjective meaning suitable; it is the verb, STEAL, which is said like STEEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel blue is a greyish-blue shade, so it names a tone of colour.

clue.text: Foam covering European potato skin is unwelcome grub

indicators.note: covering means wrapped round, so the foam encloses the letter

parts.note: lather is the foam of soap and water
a jacket potato is one baked in its skin, so jacket is a potato's skin

explanation.surface: Food made from foamed European potato skins isn't welcome on the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grub' looks like food but means a larva. A jacket potato is the British name for a baked potato.
explanation.definitionFit: A leatherjacket is the larva of the crane fly, a grub that eats lawn and crop roots, so gardeners dread it.

clue.text: Kindly try cuddling partner following offer

indicators.note: following means the later pieces come after the first one in the answer

parts.note: a tender is a formal offer, as in a bid for a contract
to hear a case is to try it in court
a ted is short for a teddy bear, a child's partner for cuddling

explanation.surface: A gentle soul tries cuddling a partner after making an offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuddling' looks like it tells one piece to hold another; it belongs with 'partner', a teddy, cut down to TED.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender-hearted person is gentle and sympathetic, which is what kindly describes as an adjective.

clue.text: Try bulb son damaged in obdurate fashion

indicators.note: damaged means broken, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stubbornly keeps trying a bulb their son broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges TRY, BULB and SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Obdurate means unyielding, so acting in an obdurate fashion is acting stubbornly.

clue.text: Fetch editor after retired informer is identified as victim

indicators.note: after means the following pieces are placed later than the first in the answer
retired suggests drawing back, so the word is turned round to run backwards

parts.note: a rat is slang for an informer who betrays associates
to fetch something is to go and get it

explanation.surface: An informer, now retired, finds himself marked out as a victim once the editor is fetched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' signals the reversal and 'after' puts the fetching and the editor behind it; the definition is the three-word phrase at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone targeted has been singled out and picked as the object of an attack or campaign.

clue.text: Two articles about bishop of ancient city

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the articles go round the next piece

parts.note: the definite article THE and the indefinite article AN
B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A historian writes two articles on a bishop of some ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of ancient city' defines an adjective: something belonging to Thebes.
explanation.definitionFit: Theban is the adjective for Thebes, the ancient Greek (or Egyptian) city.

clue.text: Maybe trunks of wood pronounced over river

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so this part comes first
pronounced means said out loud, so the word is spelt as it sounds

parts.note: beech is a hardwood timber
the Wear is a river in north-east England, through Durham

explanation.surface: Wooden trunks, perhaps tree trunks, are said to lie across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunks' looks like tree trunks, fitting 'wood'; they are swimming trunks.
explanation.definitionFit: Swimming trunks are an example of what one wears on the sand, hence 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Sorry fellow more disheartened coming below average

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming below means placed underneath, so these pieces follow the first

parts.note: par is the normal or average level, as in 'below par'
a don is a fellow of a college at Oxford or Cambridge

indicators.note: disheartened means losing the heart, so the middle letters go and only the outer pair stays

explanation.surface: A fellow who is more downhearted after a below-average result says sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: MORE loses its heart, OR, to leave ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Pardon me is a polite apology or a request to repeat, used just as one says sorry.

clue.text: Reptile mostly black going to the West Country

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west means running right to left, so the letters are read backwards
mostly means most but not all of the word, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: a lizard is a reptile
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencil grades

explanation.surface: A reptile, mostly black, heads for the West Country, the south-west of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West Country' looks like one place; 'the West' is the reversal and 'Country' alone is the definition. LIZAR plus B is LIZARB, which 'going to the West' reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Brazil is the largest country in South America.

clue.text: Parts of course of airway staff only partly required

indicators.note: only partly signals that the answer is a part of the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: Airline staff are only partly needed on some sections of a training course.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'oF AIRWAY Staff'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairways are the mown stretches of a golf course between tee and green.

clue.text: Awful option, fan had to bear English having dire penalties

indicators.note: to bear is to carry, so the shuffled letters hold the next piece
awful suggests something botched or mangled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fan who had a dreadful option must put up with English rules carrying dire penalties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' shuffles the three words into ONPAINOFDATH, and 'to bear' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule made on pain of death carries execution as the punishment for breaking it, the direst penalty.

clue.text: Member of abbey busybody reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, so the word is taken for its sound

parts.note: a prier is one who pries, a nosy busybody

explanation.surface: A meddling busybody informs on a monk of the abbey.
explanation.walkthrough: PRIER and the answer are said alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A prior is a monk ranking just below an abbot, so a senior member of an abbey.

clue.text: Ring useless — it's egg-shaped

parts.note: the letter O is ring-shaped
void means invalid, of no legal effect, i.e. useless

explanation.surface: An egg-shaped ring is declared worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' is a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovoid comes from Latin ovum, egg, and describes an oval, egg-like form.

clue.text: Not all drink noisily and speak like a drunk

indicators.note: not all of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to slurp is to drink noisily

explanation.surface: Not every drinker slurps, but some do and then talk like drunks.
explanation.walkthrough: SLURP loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To slur words is to run them together indistinctly, typical of a drunk's speech.

clue.text: Clearly establishes claws and feathers

definitions.meaning: to nail down a fact is to settle or establish it firmly
nails are claws and down is soft feathers, read as two nouns

explanation.surface: Something clearly settles the matter of claws and feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as two separate nouns, NAILS and DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nailing something down means fixing it securely, so a fact nailed down is firmly established.

clue.text: Fall on joint securing middle of panel in boat

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the outer word wraps round the letter

parts.note: a keel is a flat-bottomed boat, used on the Tyne

indicators.note: the middle of a five-letter word is its third letter

explanation.surface: A worker falls on a joint while fixing the central panel inside a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of 'panel' is N, held in KEEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To kneel is to drop down onto one's knees, and the knee is a joint.

clue.text: Shelter you refit after removing all contents

indicators.note: emptying a word of its contents leaves only its outer letters, here applied to both words

explanation.surface: A camper is told to refit their shelter once everything inside has been cleared out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you' emptied is YU and 'refit' emptied is RT.
explanation.definitionFit: A yurt is a round felt tent of Central Asian nomads, a portable dwelling or shelter.

clue.text: Returned a novel about very intrepid sort

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the next piece
novel means new, so these letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone returns a novel about a very brave hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' looks like a reversal signal, but it is the fodder for 'novel', which shuffles it to DENTURER; 'about' puts V inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventurer is one who seeks out daring exploits, a bold and intrepid type.
